Hi All,
After plenty of assistance from the group (and thanks to Dan Linden for code) I have managed to get my data into shape for gpcount().  see below for summary of the unmarked frame.  I have sampled forest birds across a temperature gradient, within 2 seasons, and with years grouped in two time steps of about 8 and 6 years respectively.  I am interested to detect differences between the two time-steps.  My question is: What is the best way to estimate abundance across the gradient within each time-step? should I be using predict() or ranef(), as has sometimes been suggested?  How do I specify which is the time_step variable when using ranef?  any poiters to examples or code would be much appreciated.
Cheers

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: gpcount(), estimating difference in abundance between primary periods
parts: I'm not sure if you can extract posteriors for the primary periods from a gpcount model, but generally you are not interested in estimates for the primary periods because you are assuming that the abundance at a site does not change across primary & secondary periods.  The reason there is variation in your observed counts is due to differences in availability and detectability.  The ecological process of interest is abundance, which can only be site specific in a gpcount model.  You need to use pcountOpen if you want period-specific estimates of abundance.

messages.author: 1cab2db425f24b0c
messages.subject: Re: gpcount(), estimating difference in abundance between primary periods
parts:
Hey all! 

I am also working with an 'unmarkedFramGPC' dataframe and am using 'gpcount' to fit my models. I understand that the predict() function used on the top model outputs M(i) for each site. I am just following up on this chain to ask three quick questions: 
  1. I'm looking at the likelihood of the Chandler et al. (2011) model and because availability varies over time, I must have different estimates of available abundance for each primary period that are informing M(i), right? Is the site-specific M(i) an average of the N(i,t)'s? 

  2. In AHM volume 1 (Kery and Royle 2016), it is noted that the Chandler et al. (2011) model had been extended to fit binomial mixture models for repeated counts, and the R help file for '?gpcount' specifies that the function "fits the model of Chandler et al. (2011) to repeated count data collected using the robust design." Am I correct in assuming the robust design is the two-tiered design that assumes population closure within primary periods and an open population between prim. periods? 

  3. I'm curious if there have been any changes/extensions have been made to extract posteriors for the primary periods to retrieve N(i,t) since this thread was opened?
I want to ensure I understand the conceptual foundation of where my estimates are coming from, and get a gauge on how/if I can estimate the N(i,t) values. I know people aren't often interested in the primary-period abundance estimates, but it is relevant to my study system (as we believe there are seasonal fluctuations), and I am interested in comparing N-mixture prim. pd. estimates to my CMR prim. pd. estimates. 

Respectfully,
Megan Novak
